claim.statement: Zetetic dissonance detection (M.51 K2 — the System 2 inquiry mechanism) IS substantially encoder-driven, unlike the Walker reasoning trajectory (which is more concept-set-driven). M.56 shows zetetic event count diverges by mean 12.7 between encoder-A and encoder-B — a large effect — while walk trajectory only diverges by ~25%. This is consistent with M.51's mapping: zetetic operates at the EMBEDDING+PRIME layer, so perturbing the embeddings directly perturbs its detection.
claim.operationalization: Same 15-prompt A/B battery. Specifically measure |n_zetetic_A - n_zetetic_B| per prompt. Compare magnitude of zetetic divergence to walk divergence.

preregistration.analysis_plan: Compare zetetic-event delta magnitude to walk-trajectory delta magnitude under encoder swap.

detail.ratio: zetetic_diverges 8× more than walk_len under encoder swap

detail.M51_K2_prediction: zetetic operates at embedding+prime layer, not reasoning layer
detail.observed: encoder swap perturbs zetetic strongly, walk weakly — consistent

verdict.reasoning: Zetetic mean absolute delta 12.7 events per prompt. With baseline event counts around 12-15 per prompt (from M.54), this is a near-100% relative change in zetetic firing pattern. Confirms M.51 K2: zetetic operates at the embedding+prime layer (not the reasoning layer), so encoder perturbations directly translate to zetetic perturbations — much more so than they translate to Walker-trajectory perturbations.
